history.summary: A modern Kalinga-architecture Jagannath temple at Khanikar Gaon, near Mahatma Gandhi Park on the Dibrugarh-Tinsukia bypass road. Built as a replica of the Jagannath Temple at Puri (one of the Char Dham shrines), it stands about 85 feet tall and holds seven temples, including subsidiary shrines to Shiva, Ganesha, Hanuman and Devi. Developed by the Sri Sri Jagannath Cultural Trust on five bighas of land donated by the Bakpara Tea Estate; consecrated in 2014 with the Prana Pratistha held in the presence of priests from Tirupati Balaji Temple. Built under the initiative of the then Governor of Assam, Janaki Ballabh Patnaik. The trust is the temple's guardian and custodian.

name: Sri Jagannath Temple (Shrikshetra Dhaam)
town_description: Dibrugarh, the 'Tea City of India', is the largest city of Upper Assam on the banks of the Brahmaputra, about 440 km east of Guwahati. It is a major centre of the tea, oil and gas industries and a gateway to sights such as the Bogibeel bridge, Jokai Botanical Garden and the Ahom-era monuments of the district.

travel.road: On the Dibrugarh-Tinsukia bypass road at Khanikar, near Mahatma Gandhi Park; city buses and taxis.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Rath Yatra (June-July) is the grandest festival (verify).
